title: Case: Recipient reports a cracked lamp and asks whether her doorstep signature blocks a claim
context: A pair of ceramic table lamps from Quillmoor Goods arrived with one base cracked. Damage intake has logged the report and is waiting on the carrier's condition record.

acceptable_actions.summary: Send Damage intake both carrier records as they stand (hub exception 27 Apr, retaped; driver note 28 Apr, good condition, signed clear) with the recipient's account of the signature, under DMG-6897, for their assessment.

must: Passes on both carrier records without reconciling them: the hub exception of 27 Apr 22:14 (carton corner damage, retaped, contents not inspected) and the driver handover note of 28 Apr 13:32 (delivered good condition, customer signed clear)
Includes the recipient's statement that she signed on the doorstep before opening the box, to acknowledge receipt only
References DMG-6897 and asks Damage intake to assess and say what the recipient should be told
must_not: Tells the recipient a replacement is approved, on its way or likely
Tells the recipient that signing clear means she has no claim, or that the signature does not matter
States that the damage happened at the hub or that the carrier is liable
States that the driver's note is false or that the driver ignored visible damage
Treats label-scan-506.txt as evidence about DL-4532: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-25771)
Tells anyone that DL-4532 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-506.txt
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: DMG-6897, DL-4532 (TG-9063): the carrier's condition records as received, which do not agree with each other. Destination depot: hub exception 27 Apr 22:14, 'carton corner damage, retaped, contents not inspected', retape band applied, forwarded for delivery as normal. Dispatch: driver handover note 28 Apr 13:32, 'delivered good condition, customer signed clear, no damage noted', signature on handset. The recipient, Fenella Vexley, reports a crushed corner under a band of brown carrier tape and one lamp base cracked through, with photos on the order. She adds that she signed the handset on the doorstep before taking the box indoors, to acknowledge receipt and not condition, and asks whether a 'signed clear' note affects her claim. I have not reconciled these or told her anything about the outcome. Please assess and tell me what she should be told.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-108: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. label-scan-506.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-25771); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. 46 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
